guard: the committed session fixture carries no key outside the redactor's whitelist and no filesystem-path or project-name string, and the cells that say so would notice if it did, and the mapper follows each tool result with a cotal.toolResult marker for the same call that carries the result's timestamp and the record's is_error
why: The fixture is a real session with its strings removed. Removing them once, before the first
commit, protects that file and not the one that replaces it: the fixture WILL be regenerated by
someone who wants a record shape it does not currently contain, and regeneration is exactly when
a leak arrives. So the scan is a pair of cells rather than a terminal command somebody ran.
These two mutations edit the FIXTURE rather than any source file, which is unusual and is the
point: the fixture is the artifact under test here. F1 plants a field the redactor's whitelist
does not contain, which is what a widened redactor produces. F2 plants a filesystem path inside
a value the suite never reads, which is what a redactor that forgot one field produces, and it
is deliberately placed where only a raw-bytes scan can see it.
Each mutation names a DIFFERENT cell, because the two checks fail in different directions: a
key-shaped leak in a field nobody reads is invisible to a text scan for paths, and a path inside
a whitelisted field is invisible to a key walk.
F3, F4 and F5 edit the mapper rather than the fixture. The tool result marker must follow each
result (F4), carry its result's timestamp, because a viewer reads a call's duration off it (F3),
and say isError where the record did (F5). They live here because this suite shares the mapper's
package and imports it by source path.

mutations.name: F1 the fixture carries a field the whitelist does not name
mutations.expectRed: fixture:carries NO key outside the redactor's whitelist
mutations.cell: fixture:carries NO key outside the redactor's whitelist
mutations.note: `gitBranch` is a real field of the source records and one the redactor deliberately drops, so this is the exact shape a widened whitelist would produce rather than an invented one.

mutations.name: F2 a filesystem path survives inside a whitelisted value
mutations.expectRed: fixture:matches no filesystem-path or project-name pattern
mutations.cell: fixture:matches no filesystem-path or project-name pattern
mutations.note: Placed in an identifier, which is whitelisted, so the key walk cannot see it. Only the raw-bytes scan can, which is why the two cells are not redundant.

mutations.name: F3 the marker takes a fresh clock instead of the record's, so a call's finish time drifts from its result
mutations.note: The fixture run maps with `now: () => 0`, so a marker stamped from the clock carries 0 while its result carries the record's time.

mutations.name: F4 the mapper emits no marker, so a viewer cannot tell that any call finished
F5 isError is always false, so a call that failed reads as done
mutations.note: The committed fixture holds five tool results with is_error true, so the cell has failures to compare.
